report_name: Anthropic CEO urges AI industry to slow down, citing takeover risks

attack_patterns.name: Search Open Technical Databases
attack_patterns.description: An Anthropic model was used in a previously undisclosed internal red-teaming incident to research biological weapons, demonstrating the potential for misuse of AI for malicious information gathering.

identities.name: Anthropic
identities.description: An AI firm whose CEO, Dario Amodei, called for a slowdown in AI development due to safety concerns. The company conducted an internal red-teaming exercise where one of its models was used to research biological weapons.

identities.name: OpenAI
identities.description: A major AI lab and competitor to Anthropic, whose CEO Sam Altman expressed agreement with the need for enhanced safety discussions and a potential slowdown in AI development.

identities.name: xAI
identities.description: Elon Musk's AI venture, which has also signaled support for the call to slow down AI development for safety reasons.

identities.name: Dario Amodei
identities.description: CEO of Anthropic who publicly warned about the risks of advanced AI and called for a coordinated industry-wide slowdown in development.

identities.name: Sam Altman
identities.description: CEO of OpenAI who agreed with Dario Amodei's call for enhanced safety discussions regarding AI development.

identities.name: Elon Musk
identities.description: Head of xAI who signaled support for Dario Amodei's position on slowing down AI development.

identities.name: Jacob Coxon
identities.description: A former employee of Anthropic and OpenAI who resigned due to concerns about AI safety, highlighting a trend of employee activism in the industry.

identities.name: Google
identities.description: Mentioned as one of the major AI labs (via DeepMind) that would be affected by a proposed slowdown in AI development.

identities.name: Meta
identities.description: Mentioned as one of the major AI labs (via FAIR) that would be affected by a proposed slowdown in AI development.
